options.name: Cone-mode sparse working tree
options.description: Initial checkout materializes repository-root files rather than the entire repository, reducing client-side checkout and working-tree overhead.

options.name: Full working-tree population
options.description: The complete repository working tree is materialized when a client requires all files locally.

options.name: Minimized populated working set
options.description: Client materialization prioritizes minimizing populated files because file data dominates working-tree cost.

options.name: Virtualized filesystem materialization
options.description: A virtualized filesystem defers populated working-tree updates and presents missing content on demand.

options.name: On-demand working-tree expansion
options.description: Additional repository areas are materialized only when clients request them, avoiding unnecessary initial checkout work.

options.name: Background registered-repository maintenance
options.description: Repositories receive scheduled background maintenance after registration, including commit-graph and object-maintenance tasks.

options.name: Foreground explicit maintenance
options.description: Users invoke maintenance directly or through a user-controlled schedule, including a command that runs all maintenance steps.

options.name: User-controlled maintenance suspension
options.description: Users can pause or unregister repositories to suspend or stop background optimization work.

options.name: Coalesced bookkeeping updates
options.description: Related bookkeeping reference updates are combined into fewer transactions.

options.name: Priority scheduling for user updates
options.description: User-initiated reference updates are scheduled ahead of noncritical bookkeeping work.

options.name: Quiescing before planned reboot
options.description: Planned maintenance drains long-running reads before a server is rebooted.

options.name: Continued write delivery during quiescing
options.description: Writes continue reaching a quiescing replica so it does not fall arbitrarily behind before returning online.

options.name: Abrupt reboot without read draining
options.description: A server is rebooted or unplugged without allowing active reads to finish.

options.name: Rolling reboot testing
options.description: Controlled rack-by-rack rolling reboots test failure handling while limiting disruption.

options.name: Five-server rack reboot concurrency
options.description: No more than five servers in a rack are rebooted concurrently after quiescing.

options.name: Offline marking for new read operations
options.description: Marks a quiescing server unavailable for new reads while allowing existing operations to drain.

options.name: Loose-object storage
options.description: Each newly created object is stored as a separate file, favoring quick creation but accumulating storage and performance overhead.

options.name: Compressed pack-file object storage
options.description: Git objects are stored in compressed pack files, including size-minimizing and delta-compressed layouts.

options.name: Incremental pack-file repacking
options.description: Small batches of packs are rewritten incrementally, limiting pack counts while avoiding an impractical full repository rewrite.

options.name: Single-pack full rewrite
options.description: All repository data is rewritten into one pack-file, an explicitly rejected approach when repository size makes the rewrite inefficient.

options.name: Two-phase pack expiration
options.description: New packs are indexed and references redirected before obsolete packs are deleted, reducing disruption to concurrent foreground operations.

options.name: Full object-data rewrite maintenance
options.description: Repository upkeep completely rewrites and recompresses object data rather than maintaining it incrementally.

options.name: S3-backed write-ahead log
options.description: Durable repository state is kept in S3, allowing local repository copies to be recreated on any host.

options.name: Relational repository-location database
options.description: A relational database tracks repository locations; Continuity explicitly rejects operating such a database for authoritative placement state.

options.name: Cloud-portable object-storage deployment
options.description: Deploy the durable object-storage log on any compatible cloud rather than one provider.

options.name: Fast-NVMe local Git repository
options.description: Keep a normal Git repository on fast local NVMe storage for upstream Git compatibility and performance.

options.name: Centralized repository hosting
options.description: Repositories are hosted through a central service while clients may retain distributed Git capabilities.

options.name: Stateless rendezvous-hash placement
options.description: Healthy-node rendezvous hashing identifies expected repository locations without maintaining authoritative routing tables.

options.name: Authoritative routing-table placement
options.description: A maintained per-repository routing table determines repository locations; this stateful alternative is rejected in favor of stateless placement.

options.name: External repository-to-machine routing database
options.description: A separate database tracks the machines holding each repository replica.

options.name: Arbitrary-server write primaries
options.description: Any server can receive a push and act as primary, with S3 compare-and-swap synchronizing concurrent WAL updates.

options.name: Rendezvous-ranked preferred primary
options.description: The highest-ranked healthy server is normally preferred to reduce compare-and-swap retries while preserving correctness if another server receives the write.

options.name: Optimistic gossip dissemination
options.description: Replicas exchange catch-up metadata through lossy UDP gossip and independently recover missing data from S3.

options.name: Asynchronous compacted-pack fan-out
options.description: Distribute primary-produced compacted packs through shared object storage instead of locally repacking replicas.

options.name: Git-and-rsync replication mechanism
options.description: Combine Git-aware and rsync-based mechanisms for repository replication, repair, and rebalancing.

options.name: Proxy-mediated multi-fileserver replication
options.description: Send each Git push through a proxy that replicates it across multiple fileservers.

options.name: Unsynchronized packfile fan-out
options.description: Large pushed packfiles are sent to replicas without consensus; only the smaller reference publication is synchronized.

options.name: Spokes repository replication
options.description: A purpose-built repository replication system replaces latency-sensitive block-level filesystem duplication.

options.name: WAL-indexed local reference publication
options.description: Publish references after a local transaction succeeds and its WAL pointer is recorded.

options.name: Reference-transaction consensus boundary
options.description: Consensus synchronizes the small reference transaction that publishes pushed objects, not the large packfile.

options.name: Fully consistent replica cluster
options.description: Replicas maintain identical repository state and can all serve reads and repository operations.

options.name: Eventually consistent repository views
options.description: Replicas may temporarily expose divergent repository state after writes.

options.name: Three-phase commit synchronization
options.description: A coordinator directs replicas through prepare, commit, or rollback for synchronized reference updates.

options.name: Per-write voting protocol
options.description: Run a vote for each write to determine its winning order and outcome without a fixed primary.

options.name: Single-primary write ordering
options.description: Use one designated primary replica to establish the official order of every write.

options.name: Majority-based write durability
options.description: Treat a write as durable after acceptance by a replica majority.

options.name: Rollback of non-majority writes
options.description: Revert writes that fail to apply identically at a replica majority.

options.name: Two-copy replica strategy
options.description: Maintaining two copies provides tolerance for a single node failure but is rejected in favor of majority-based replication.

options.name: Minimum two-copy synchronous durability
options.description: Writes require synchronous storage on at least two replicas before acceptance.

options.name: Refusal of under-replicated writes
options.description: Writes are rejected when the required synchronous replica durability cannot be achieved.

options.name: Acceptance without safe commit
options.description: Writes are accepted despite lacking the required durable synchronous replication.

options.name: Read-preserving write optimization
options.description: Write-scaling changes preserve read performance despite reads greatly outnumbering writes.

options.name: Non-voting geo-replica hosts
options.description: Geographically replicated hosts remain non-voting so unreachable replicas do not block primary-host pushes.

options.name: Durability-before-acknowledgment push handling
options.description: Acknowledge pushes only after their durable log entries have been fully persisted.

options.name: Per-push WAL object storage
options.description: Represent each push as a separate durable object while the pushed pack is uploaded separately.

options.name: Batched object-storage writes
options.description: Batch log writes to avoid object-storage request latency limiting ingestion throughput.

options.name: Three-way repository replication
options.description: Maintain three repository replicas so an up-to-date copy remains available after a server failure.

options.name: Geographically distributed repository replicas
options.description: Place repository replicas across separated datacenters for disaster survivability and regional reads.

options.name: Consistency and partition-tolerance priority
options.description: Replication prioritizes consistency and partition tolerance over uninterrupted availability during failures.

options.name: Isolation of losing replicas
options.description: Make replicas on the losing side of a write vote unavailable until repaired.

options.name: Automatic replica repair
options.description: Unhealthy or divergent repository copies are detected and repaired automatically or rapidly.

options.name: N-to-N replica reconstruction
options.description: Rebuild replacement replicas anywhere using any surviving replicas as sources.

options.name: Rapid repository repair scheduling
options.description: Unhealthy repository copies are quickly detected and scheduled for repair because corruption equals loss of a copy.

options.name: Graceful server retirement through replica removal
options.description: A retiring server is removed from the active replica count while remaining available during automated replacement.

options.name: Incremental XOR state checksum
options.description: Reference-value hashes are incrementally added and removed to compare logical replica state efficiently after updates.

options.name: From-scratch checksum recomputation
options.description: Recomputing the checksum from every reference after each update is rejected because it limits update throughput.

options.name: Single-replica read routing
options.description: Reads and clones use any one up-to-date replica rather than combining reads across replicas.

options.name: Replica-based read scale-out
options.description: An arbitrary number of repository replicas serve read-only operations horizontally without relaxing consistency.

options.name: Replica-based distributed locking
options.description: Replicas act as distributed locks to order coordinated database updates.

options.name: Overlapped work during replica waits
options.description: Computation, locking, checksums, or reads proceed while coordination messages are in flight.

options.name: Closest synchronized-replica routing
options.description: Reads are sent to an up-to-date replica selected by geographic or preference proximity.

options.name: Operation-level replica failover
options.description: Each failed operation retries another preferred repository replica.

options.name: Preference-ordered replica lists
options.description: Routing returns multiple current replicas in an order suitable for fallback.

options.name: Co-located GVFS cache server
options.description: A nearby cache server handles GVFS requests for sufficiently large repositories serving large user groups.

options.name: GVFS without cache infrastructure
options.description: Using GVFS without the required cache-server infrastructure is explicitly rejected as unsuitable for the relevant deployment conditions.

options.name: Standard Git protocol
options.description: Repositories without sufficient resources or scale for GVFS infrastructure use an existing Git-protocol endpoint instead.

options.name: Warm-cache repository retention
options.description: Local repository copies remain as warm caches and are rematerialized from the WAL after idle-state eviction.

options.name: Horizontally scaled application servers
options.description: Repository-facing application instances scale out to support more features and users.

options.name: Virtualized filesystem for large repositories
options.description: Use a virtualized filesystem to scale client access beyond ordinary repository-size assumptions.

options.name: Native Git optimization without virtualization
options.description: Scale large repositories through native Git improvements without requiring a virtualized filesystem.

options.name: Recommended Git configuration tuning
options.description: Apply recommended Git configuration automatically to improve command performance across repository shapes.

options.name: Centralized on-demand object retrieval
options.description: A central service supplies missing Git objects as clients request them, relaxing full distribution for scale.

options.name: Partial commit-tree initial clone
options.description: Initial clones transfer commits and trees while omitting other Git objects until needed.

options.name: Commit-graph acceleration
options.description: Commit-graph generation and verification accelerate history operations in large repositories.

options.name: Background remote fetching
options.description: Repositories periodically fetch remote updates in the background rather than relying only on user-initiated fetches.

options.name: Source repository under /src
options.description: Client repositories are placed under a source root so generated build artifacts remain outside the repository.

options.name: Partial-clone protocol integration
options.description: Client object retrieval uses Git's partial-clone interface to integrate large-repository transfer behavior.

options.name: Hidden remote-reference namespace
options.description: Background fetch stores remote references under a private namespace without changing normal remote-tracking references.

options.name: Foreground remote-reference update fetch
options.description: Users explicitly fetch in the foreground when remote-tracking references must be updated.

options.name: Packfile network interchange
options.description: Push and fetch operations exchange compressed packfiles regardless of internal repository handling.

options.name: Failure-aware request routing
options.description: Route repository requests around unavailable or degraded servers.

options.name: Combined heartbeat and application-traffic monitoring
options.description: Detect failures using both heartbeats and real Git application requests.

options.name: Heartbeat-only health checking
options.description: Use only heartbeat reachability to detect server failures.

options.name: Three-consecutive-failure offline threshold
options.description: Mark a node offline only after three consecutive failed requests.

options.name: RPC-failover graph diagnosis
options.description: Failover graphs expose an application server whose detector incorrectly marks all file servers offline.

options.name: RPC failure-based node detection
options.description: Connection refusals and timeouts are the primary signals that a server is unavailable.

options.name: Secondary heartbeat polling
options.description: Heartbeats provide load information and recovery all-clear signals rather than primary failure detection.

options.name: Per-application-server failure views
options.description: Each application server maintains its own observed offline list for file servers.

options.name: Cross-server failure correlation
options.description: Observations across application servers distinguish file-server faults from application-server faults.

options.name: Auxiliary Scalar acceleration layer
options.description: A service-agnostic Scalar layer accelerates repositories while Git lacks required native capabilities.

options.name: Core Git native acceleration
options.description: Large-repository acceleration capabilities are integrated into the core Git client instead of remaining in a separate layer.

options.name: Custom Git distribution
options.description: The acceleration layer is delivered through a custom Git build until its features are available in core Git.

options.name: Per-repository optimization registration
options.description: Repositories explicitly opt into client-side optimization and its associated local configuration and maintenance.

options.name: GVFS Protocol acceleration
options.description: Scalar uses the legacy GVFS Protocol for performance when the hosting service supports it.

options.name: Scalar-local performance implementation
options.description: Advanced performance capabilities are implemented only in Scalar rather than in standard Git.

options.name: GVFS Protocol in standard Git
options.description: The legacy GVFS Protocol is extended into the standard Git client.

options.name: Compatibility-preserving opt-in optimization
options.description: Advanced performance features remain disabled by default and require explicit configuration to preserve compatibility.

options.name: Shared team performance configuration
options.description: Customized Git performance settings are centrally shared across team machines.

options.name: Local on-disk Git repository access
options.description: Standard Git operations execute against a repository stored on local disk or a dedicated host's local filesystem.

options.name: Replicated network filesystem access
options.description: Repository files are exposed through block- or file-level replicated network filesystems.

options.name: RPC dedicated-fileserver access
options.description: An application accesses repositories on dedicated fileservers through RPC rather than distributing the filesystem itself.

options.name: Block-level replicated filesystem
options.description: Repository data is duplicated through block-level filesystem replication between closely placed machines.

options.name: HTTP daemon over on-disk repository
options.description: A conventional HTTP daemon directly fronts a repository stored on one disk or machine.

options.name: Filesystem-level repository distribution
options.description: Repository files are distributed beneath the application without changing Git or packfile semantics.

options.name: Untransformed Git repository data
options.description: Hosting retains ordinary Git repository data rather than converting it to a service-specific representation.

options.name: Git-aware filesystem watcher
options.description: A watcher integrated with Git filters irrelevant changes and avoids unnecessary working-tree scans.

options.name: Git fsmonitor integration
options.description: Git obtains modified paths through an fsmonitor integration instead of scanning all populated paths.

options.name: Watchman-backed filesystem monitoring
options.description: An external Watchman service supplies filesystem changes to Git for large working trees.

options.name: Full working-directory scan
options.description: Git discovers changes by scanning every populated path without filesystem monitoring.

options.name: Sequential Git DAG traversal
options.description: Repository operations follow commit, tree, and file links step by step rather than independently resolving objects.

options.name: Distributed object-store Git repository
options.description: Git objects are resolved through a distributed key-value or DHT-backed store instead of conventional repository storage.

options.name: Multi-pack index tracking
options.description: A multi-pack index tracks objects across packs without requiring all repository data to be rewritten into one pack.

options.name: Distributed Git collaboration workflow
options.description: Contributors retain decentralized maintainer, offline-work, and delayed-push capabilities while repositories may still be hosted centrally.

options.name: Centralized hosted collaboration workflow
options.description: Contributors use a central repository host as the primary collaboration point while Git remains available to users.
